checks: Exact rational subtraction gives the listed monotone lower and upper endpoint increments. Linear interpolation produces the four actual fibers. Their lengths sum to 211/50, and the interval central second moments give the variance 1937167/6330000.

Independently generated all six clipping breakpoints at each inner base by dividing both endpoints of each exterior interval by z−p. Fraction arithmetic reproduced all twelve listed values, the constant tails, and the minimum Q in both orientations. Since the cap profile is affine between these knots and a nonvertical boundary has zero length, this checks every nonvertical slope. The two least closed pure-base masses are 11/5 and 101/50.

Direct endpoint substitution verifies the four attaining caps have original mass 11/10, with only the own trace proper. The smallest absolute exterior status margin is 1/100. A nonnegative shift of at most 1/10000 changes each attaining cap's own length by precisely the shift and preserves exterior statuses. Every other cap through either mark gains at least that own-fiber amount, and the pure-base minimum remains larger.

For an inner mark with 0<|y|≤1/1000, use the cap of its pair with the sign facing y. Its external statuses persist because |y|+delta≤11/10000<1/100, so the bound is Q−|y|+delta(y). The local Lipschitz constant below one yields strict loss from its own zero mark. At larger inner |y| the fixed tightening by 1/1000 gives ordinary depth at most Q−1/1000. At exterior bases a finite exposing slope isolates each own interval, giving ordinary depth at most 9/100. At any mark the shift gains at most four times its size on every nonvertical cap, while pure-base caps are unchanged. The resulting exterior upper bound is strictly below Q.

Direct subtraction after the one-dimensional projective change gives the original interval length divided by the product of the two admissible endpoint denominators. That product is a strictly concave quadratic whose maximum lies between its two zeros, giving E(y)=4(y−l)(u−y)/(u−l), also at endpoints by extension. Exact arithmetic gives E1=44/21, E2=46/25, E1'(0)=−4/21 and a=−1/22. The endpoint and derivative bounds over both closed inner neighborhoods give E_i>1 and |E_i'|<1.

Since E_p(y)/M<1, Sigma<1, and 0<r≤1, the cap shift is at most epsilon and the derivative magnitude on each inner neighborhood is strictly below epsilon. The first marked shift is strictly larger. The designated active pair remains proper only on the source and hence regular. Its unit signed normals have weights summing to one and difference delta_1'(0); the two weights are positive. The projective substitution changes the resultant to (2r−1)delta_1(0)a, which is nonzero when r differs from one half.

Source 75dd33535e246a34 §§1–3 supplies the exact ordinary construction and tables. Source 1298c8ea2c6ec3df §§1–3 calibrates the r=1/2 case, with its regular pair in §4. Source 3101206ec4580190 §5 extends to the interval 0<r≤1, and the frozen proof establishes the uniform small-shift criterion directly.

overlap.comparison: The general strict ordinary depth interpolation allows two adjacent maximizing bases in one integer coordinate. It does not specify this exact family, its all-normal depth, the positive-buffer winner, or the projective resultant.

The accepted positive-buffer example has three identical interval fibers and uses an affine multiplier to create supporting minimizers. Its assumptions and maximizing set differ from this four-interval, unweighted-power, regular-cap calculation.

readability: The clipping table and ordinary tails specify all slopes. The two active caps used at a mark are designated witnesses; the claim does not require uniqueness of their slopes.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The exact through-mark cap tables, finite margin witnesses, and all-source comparison certify the ordinary tie and the buffered selection for every stated exponent and shift.
